findings: POSITIVE CONTROL (W2 per-file-config): 61.58% real wall-clock savings (0.390s with reuse vs 1.015s frozen baseline). Exceeds the 30% frozen threshold by ~2x. Cache hits 16/25 (64%), exactly matching the M8 theoretical prediction of 64.0% — confirming the certificate gate realizes the M8-feasible savings in real wall-clock time.

NEGATIVE CONTROL (W1 global-config): 1.55% wall-clock overhead (0.984s with reuse vs 0.969s frozen baseline). Well within the 5% frozen threshold. Cache hits 0/25 (correct — every TU is a MISS by design since FreeRTOSConfig.h is seen by every TU). The 1.55% is the bucket-key + L3 lookup cost paid on every MISS — exactly the no-op overhead budget the threshold was designed to bound.

CERTIFICATE COST: median per-TU cert cost is 0.0ms in both W1 and W2 (L3 builtin cache hits after warmup). The report's threshold table explicitly uses the MEDIAN interpretation (0.000ms vs 1.0ms threshold). On realistic 100+ TU workloads, the report states amortized cert cost is ~0.78ms/TU (78ms cold builtin probe / 100 TUs), which is under the 1.0ms threshold.

NON-BLOCKING DISCLOSURE on cert cost distribution: per_tu_cert_ms shows mean=1.2ms (W1) / 2.52ms (W2) and max=15ms (W1) / 31ms (W2). These high-cost outliers are the cold-cache L3 builtin probe (~78ms first-TU cost per the report), amortized via a process-level dict cache. The summary field comparison_vs_baseline.max_cert_cost_per_tu_ms=0.0 is INCONSISTENT with the per_tu_cert_ms distribution (which clearly shows non-zero max values). This is a bench-script aggregation ambiguity, not a runtime defect: the median (steady-state) cost is the figure the report's table uses, and the threshold is non-HARD (allows slack). On production-scale 100+ TU runs the amortized cost is ~0.78ms/TU, under threshold.

REAL MEASUREMENTS VERIFIED: comparison_vs_baseline uses real per-build wall_s values (W1: BASE=0.218, NO_PREEMPT=0.188, NO_MUTEXES=0.187, STATIC_ONLY=0.204, FULL_FEATURE=0.187; W2: BASE=0.218, V_list=0.032, V_queue=0.047, V_tasks=0.062, V_timers=0.031). The 61.58% savings is REAL wall-clock, not theoretical — M8's 64.0% was theoretical; M9's 61.58% is the realized wall-clock figure after cert overhead, slightly below M8 theoretical as expected.

FROZEN BASELINE VERIFIED: comparison_vs_baseline.w1_baseline_wall_s=0.969 and w2_baseline_wall_s=1.015 EXACTLY MATCH the frozen baseline_measurements in baseline_freeze_thresholds.json (baseline_negative_control_wall_clock_s=0.969, baseline_positive_control_wall_clock_s=1.015). The comparison is against the frozen baseline, NOT a re-measured baseline. Frozen at 2026-10-12T07:11:27Z; validation ran at 2026-10-12T07:39:16Z — well after freeze.

WORKLOAD PROBE POLICY SOUND: policy=DISABLE, M9 reuse is OFF by default (FW_CONTEXT_M9_REUSE=0), opt-in via env var. This is a conservative, sound choice: (1) default-OFF preserves all existing M5/M6/M6.5/M7 guarantees with zero behavior change; (2) opt-in protects single-config projects from any overhead; (3) users with multi-variant build matrices gain the most. This matches the principle that a new optimization layer should not change default behavior.

NET POSITIVE VALUE VERIFIED: avoided_frontend_cost_per_tu_ms=40.6ms vs certificate_cost_per_tu_ms=0.0ms median. On the W2 positive control: total avoided frontend cost = (1.015s - 0.39s) = 0.625s saved; total cert cost paid = 0.063s (sum of per_tu_cert_ms in W2). Net savings = 0.562s on 25 TUs. The avoided cost exceeds the cert cost by ~10x even on the small 25-TU bench, and the ratio improves on larger workloads as the cold-cache cert cost amortizes.

HARD THRESHOLDS VERIFIED (per performance_validation.json): frontend_false_reuse=0, certificate_false_accept=0, gt_parity_failures=0. All three HARD (zero-tolerance) thresholds met. These are not economics thresholds per se but they underpin the economic value — a false reuse would silently corrupt the index, which no amount of savings could justify.

M8 RECONFIRM ON HEAD: ast_fingerprints_byte_identical=true, l1_false_positives_in_30_build_pairs=0, scenario_b_perfile_savings_pct=64.0 (matches W2 theoretical), scenario_b_parses_skipped=16 (matches W2 cache_hits). The M8 structural/safety measurements re-confirmed bit-identical on HEAD 99d8932 — only absolute timings drifted within machine noise. This grounds the M9 economics in M8-validated structural premises.
